My wheat is already in the ground since last October — I planted it right after the National Day holiday, same as everyone in my village. I have six mu of land, and it’s all in wheat. I bought the improved seed from the agricultural shop in town; it’s the same kind my sister-in-law used last year, and her wheat yielded better than mine, so I switched. I can’t read what’s on the bag, but the shopkeeper told me it’s the good kind. Before planting, I put down one big bag of compound fertilizer for each mu. When the wheat greened up in March, I spread another half bag of urea on every mu. It cost a lot, but two years ago I tried to save money on fertilizer and the wheat was short and thin, so I’d rather not risk that again. I already irrigated once in March because the spring was dry, and I’ll water two more times — once before the heads come out, and once when the grains are filling. Water costs money, so three times is all I can do. I sprayed herbicide once when the weeds came up, and I’ll spray again if I see bugs.

After I cut the wheat in early June, I’ll plant corn the same week — there’s no time to waste. My nephew has a machine that plants corn without plowing, so I won’t till between crops. I’ll buy hybrid corn seed, the kind that everyone in the village plants. For the corn, I’ll put down fertilizer at planting, and maybe topdress once if the plants look yellow. Two irrigations for the corn should be enough — July and August usually bring some rain, and I can’t afford to pump water three times. I’ll spray herbicide on the corn once after it comes up, and watch for corn borer. If my neighbor sprays for borer, I’ll spray too.

Those university students sometimes come to the village with their papers and talks, but I can’t read what they write, and my way has fed my family for twenty years. I thought about cotton, but my land is small and wheat-corn is safer. If corn prices are bad, at least I have wheat for our own flour. My husband works construction in Handan and sends money home, but my daughter is in middle school now and the costs are going up, so I need to be careful with every yuan I spend on the fields.
